node-1.label: A patient in their 70s presented with dyspnea and fatigue

node-2.label: No history of structural heart disease or hypertension

node-3.label: Medical history significant for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma diagnosed 4 years ago, treated with 8 courses of chemotherapy

node-4.label: Physical examination showed blood pressure 96/54 mm Hg and heart rate 56 bpm

why.why: Elevated NT-proBNP, mildly elevated troponin, diffuse right atrial mass on echocardiography, ECG P-wave/PR abnormalities, and PET hypermetabolism in atrial myocardium/pericardium strongly support cardiac dysfunction. The laboratory physician, radiologist, and pathologist all agree that obstructive/infiltrative cardiac involvement best explains the hypotension and bradycardia. Confidence remains 0.75 because histopathologic confirmation of the right atrial mass is still unavailable.

The DLBCL history and right atrial mass could suggest a hematologic malignancy, but no peripheral blood findings support a hematologic disorder, and all three experts localize the process to the heart. Hematologic disorder is therefore less likely; confidence remains 0.2.

Endocrine/adrenal insufficiency remains possible but untested because endocrine function tests were not obtained, and hypotension with bradycardia is compatible. However, the expert analyses conclude that the available imaging and biomarker evidence strongly favors cardiac pathology, with no supporting peripheral findings for an endocrine cause. Confidence remains 0.2.

Pulmonary disease is less likely: bradycardia is atypical for acute embolism, and the laboratory, radiology, and pathology analyses all conclude that the key findings are best explained by cardiac infiltration. Confidence remains 0.1.

node-10.label: Troponin is mildly elevated at 0.04 ng/mL

node-11.label: Echocardiography shows a diffuse medium-sized right atrial mass measuring approximately 50×22 mm

node-12.label: ECG shows P-wave and PR interval abnormalities

node-13.label: PET shows right atrial masses with increased myocardial/pericardial metabolism

node-14.label: Endocrine function tests were not obtained

node-15.label: No peripheral blood findings supporting a hematologic disorder

node-16.label: Right atrial mass/tumor infiltration (likely recurrent lymphoma) causing obstructive cardiac dysfunction

why.why: The diffuse right atrial mass (~50×22 mm) with PET hypermetabolism, elevated NT-proBNP, mild troponin elevation, and ECG P-wave/PR abnormalities in a patient with prior DLBCL strongly suggest right atrial tumor infiltration, likely recurrent lymphoma, causing obstructive cardiac dysfunction. All three experts support this as the best explanation, but the pathologist emphasizes that definitive confirmation requires histopathologic or cytologic proof from the right atrial mass, which remains unavailable despite prior retrieval attempts. Confidence remains 0.7 pending tissue/MRI confirmation.
